sex.evidence: Male NMRI mice (8 e 10 weeks) were supplied from the Laboratory Animal Center of Tzu Chi University

dosing.evidence: DOI (1 mg/kg, i.p.) or saline administration. DOI and NAC (Sigma, St. Louis, MO) were dissolved in 0.9% saline.

group_housing.evidence: housed 4 to 5 per cage in a 12 h light/dark cycle

assays.assay_description: Mice placed in an acrylic cylinder immediately after DOI (1 mg/kg, i.p.) injection; number of head twitches (rapid head movements with little/no trunk involvement) counted manually by two blinded observers for 30 min. NAC pretreatment (30, 100 mg/kg) and CPG/LY341495 used as antagonists.

application_type.evidence: CPG was administered intracerebroventricularly (i.c.v.) ... Other compounds were administered intraperitoneally (i.p.)

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were transferred from the colony room to the observation room and allowed to habituate for 30 min. After injection of DOI or saline, mice were immediately placed in an acrylic cylinder container.

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were immediately placed in an acrylic cylinder container

food_restriction.evidence: ad libitum access to water and food during the time the animals were in their home cages (no food in cylinder)

water_restriction.evidence: ad libitum access to water and food during the time the animals were in their home cages (no water in cylinder)

time_to_assay.evidence: After injection of DOI or saline, mice were immediately placed in an acrylic cylinder container.

outcomes.summary: DOI (1 mg/kg) significantly increased head twitch response. Pretreatment with NAC (100 mg/kg), but not 30 mg/kg, significantly decreased the DOI-induced head twitch response. The suppressing effect of NAC was reversed by the cystine-glutamate antiporter inhibitor CPG (100 nmol, i.c.v.) and the mGluR2 antagonist LY341495 (3 mg/kg).
outcomes.evidence: DOI (1 mg/kg) significantly increased head twitch response in mice. Pretreatment with NAC at high dose (100 mg/kg), but not low dose (30 mg/kg), significantly decreased the DOI-induced head twitch response.

B1_num_measures.evidence: The number of head twitch response ... was counted for 30 min

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: single total count over 30-min session reported

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of transitions or sequences reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Head twitch response is a pharmacologically-induced response, not a natural ethological behavior.

B5_social.evidence: mice were immediately placed in an acrylic cylinder container (alone)

B6_cognitive.evidence: HTR does not require learning or memory.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: counted ... by two observers (blind to the treatment)

D1_continuity.evidence: Head twitch response was observed for 30 min

D2_session_duration.evidence: counted for 30 min following DOI or saline administration

D3_recording_days.evidence: Single test session on one day.

judge_notes: Only the head twitch response is a scorable behavioural assay. The c-Fos/Egr-2 immunohistochemistry is a histological endpoint and the field potential recordings are ex vivo electrophysiology — both excluded per rubric.
All three candidates agreed on a single HTR assay; consolidated their fields.
B1: HTR count = 1 measure → score 0 (one of three candidates incorrectly scored 1).
Setup_habituation set to 'no' — the 30 min was room habituation, not apparatus habituation (rubric explicitly excludes room acclimation).
application_type set to 'multiple' because CPG was given i.c.v. while NAC/DOI/LY341495 were i.p. within this same assay.
Food/water_restriction: paper states ad libitum in home cage and standard short test in cylinder → 'during' (no food/water in apparatus).
